That helps her, but the model still leans slightly Republican at R+0.3, so this is a near tie.

outlook.text: Stout leads 88049 to 62038 with about 55% counted, and three of four reporting counties are ahead of pace. Bexar is the swing source: about 78% in and 3.6 points above pace, with around 53898 votes left. El Paso is essentially finished. The largest uncounted blocks are Medina, Maverick and Val Verde, with nothing reported yet. Medina needs only 34.2%, which suggests the remaining rural vote should not hurt much.

19013.text: Black Hawk is fully counted and finished ahead of win pace, above 2024 House and 2022 House. It is a big vote source and gave a solid cushion of net votes.

19171.text: Fully counted and ahead of pace. James beats Harris and the 2024 House result, though it falls a little short of the 2022 House result. Low impact.

19191.text: Winneshiek is fully counted and essentially on win pace, ahead of 2024 House but short of 2022 House. Neutral and low impact.

outlook.text: James leads by about 17,700 votes with 62% counted, and no county is behind pace. Linn is the driver, running well above its win pace with two thirds of its vote still out, which should widen the lead. Bremer, Fayette and Hardin have nothing in, but small GOP-leaning counties have been clearing the needed shift. Benton is the only reporting county running short of pace.

outlook.text: Huizenga leads and the model has him winning by about 10 points, with the alt model at R+14.1. Only 4% of the vote is in, so the picture is thin. outlook.text: Bohannan leads by about 1,300 votes with 29% counted, and 6 of 11 reporting counties are ahead of pace. Small GOP-leaning counties are running well above the shift needed. The big uncounted votes decide it: Scott has nothing in, and Johnson is only 16% counted but already running ahead of its win pace. Warren and Clinton are behind pace with sizable votes left. Neutral for now.
